newsitem.title: USA: BFS Bankorp hires banker to explore sale.
newsitem.headline: BFS Bankorp hires banker to explore sale.

text.p: BFS Bankorp said it hired investment bank Keefe, Bruyette & Woods Inc to explore strategic alternatives to enhancing shareholder value through the possible sale of the company.
BFS, parent of Bankers Federal Savings FSB, also said it has had preliminary discussions with other institutions. None of the institutions were identified.

BFS said there was no assurance discussions will result in a definitive merger agreement nor is there any assurance about the value that might be received by shareholders if there is an agreement to sell the company.

In an interview with Reuters in August, James Randall, president and chief executive, said the thift institution was in the third year of a turnaround and generating more money than it could use in its business.
He said the company was weighing whether to seek a buyer, make an acquisition or buy back stock.
In the fiscal third quarter ending June 30 BFS reported earnings of $2.5 million or $1.44 per share. For the nine months, earnings per share were $4.44.

BFS specializes in lending to the multi-family residential market. In the August interview, Randall said loan originations were up sharply reflecting a booming residential real estate market in New York City.
BFS, with total assets of $621.3 million, has five branch locations in New York City.
BFS was up three to 49-1/2 before a trading halt.
